text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: spike in container restarts in gpu-pool-5 (OOM) — ~12 restarts in 5m for pods matching runtime-prefill-*. Severity: P2. Pager: @maya (oncall). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefill-oom

maya (oncall): ack — joining now :eyes:

jae: seeing reproducible OOMs on long-context prefill jobs. Affected model: open-llm-large-v2, sequence lengths ~65k tokens. A bunch of 2-3k token prefetches look fine, long ones push memory. Customers: acme-inc (prod), devco (staging) seeing 502s and restarts.

jae: logs:
```
2026-03-18T03:02:12Z ERROR runtime: container runtime-prefill-78 - SIGKILL (OOM)
2026-03-18T03:02:11Z stderr: Cuda out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.45 GiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total; 22.4 GiB already allocated)
#0 0x7f8a1c... in cudnnLaunch
#1 0x55f2b9... in model_forward
```

maya (oncall): thanks jae. first mitigation: cordon node runtime-node-17, move prefill traffic off it, and reduce prefetch concurrency on pool-5. Running drain now.

maya (oncall): running command:```
kubectl cordon runtime-node-17
kubectl drain runtime-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

liam: can we fast-fallback to a smaller quantized variant (q4_0) for the long prompt path? That should cut mem ~40-50%.

sara: I just pushed a routing flag to the serving router to divert new prefill requests with context>32k to model-llm-large-q4 canary at 50%. Rolling now.

maya (oncall): applied patch and trimmed kvcache allocations on pool-5: set KV_CACHE_MAX_CHUNKS=64 for runtime-prefill.

eng-pager: early metrics: container restarts decreased to 2 in last 5m (was 12). Error rate for acme-inc dropped from 8% -> 1.5%. Latency for long requests increased slightly for canary but overall success rate improved.

support-bot: Notified #support with incident summary and customer list. Ticket created: SUP-4589.

jae: note — we saw a corner-case where a staged multi-part prompt triggers simultaneous prefetches that blow up aggregate memory. Need a guard to serialise multi-part prefetch or cap simultaneous KV allocations per request.

liam: agreed. adding a quick guard: if prefill_parts > 1 then max_concurrent_prefetch=1. I'll open a PR and link after.

maya (oncall): temporary state: node runtime-node-17 cordoned, pool-5 reduced concurrency, canary to q4_0 at 50% for >32k contexts, kvcache trimmed. Monitoring for 30m.

eng-pager: customer-impact summary for ops channel: acme-inc experienced ~150 failed responses (5-10% of their heavy-context traffic) between 03:00-03:10 UTC. Devco saw intermittent 502s in staging. No data exfiltration.

maya (oncall): updating incident status to "mitigated" — paging downgraded. Oncall handing to daytime rotation for follow-up. Action items:
- jae: postmortem draft, include kvcache & serialisation mitigation (ETA 24h)
- liam: PR for concurrent-prefetch guard (ETA 2h)
- infra: rebuild runtime-node-17 overnight and run mem-health check
- support: customer comms update (SUP-4589)

sara: pushing follow-up note to #incidents-summary and adding a trace link to the canary run.

incident-bot: UPDATE: severity reduced. Active pager cleared at 1769432375. Please complete post-incident form: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1769432101/form and add any logs or traces. :white_check_mark:
